item.title: Coherence-Rate Graphs and the Trainability of Quantum Neural Networks Under Noise
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hassan Ugail, Newton Howard
Every noise channel acting on a quantum neural network leaves a structural signature in the way it decays the coherences of the circuit, and this paper shows that the signature can be read before any training takes place. For the noise families that dominate practical device models, the decay rates within a charge sector of an equivariant network assemble into a weighted graph with closed-form edge weights, and the trainability behaviour of the circuit is organised by this coherence-rate graph. We prove a sufficient protection theorem on the graph, certified by a purely combinatorial construction from the circuit connectivity, we validate a predictor of the depth at which correlated noise degrades each trainable parameter, and we derive exact product laws for the measured degradation. item.description:

👤 Jianzhe Lin, Xiaolin Li, Fei Wang, Robert Douglas, Rajeshkumar Golani, Jubin Chheda
arXiv:2609.25337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dialogue failures in language models are usually framed as memory failures: context too long, summaries lossy, a constraint forgotten. We argue this misses a deeper problem: in many conversations the model does not forget, it commits too early. We call this early posterior collapse: unresolved user intent collapsing into a committed task state before ambiguity is resolved. We study it with controlled dialogue tasks in writing, planning, and coding using Gemini-2.5-Pro and Gemini-2.5-Flash.
